name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.

freshness.text: The feed gave no price time, so freshness cannot be checked.

components.label: Returns on capital
components.headline: Return on equity averaged 16.0% over the last 3 years against a 9.5% cost of equity (+6.5 points).

figures.method: net income to common / average equity

components.rubric: Average return on invested capital over the last three fiscal years minus the cost of capital (WACC): 4 at +10 points or more, 3 at +4, 2 at 0, 1 at -4, else 0. Banks and insurers use return on equity against the cost of equity.

components.label: Profitability and margins
components.reason: An operating margin on reported revenue does not describe a bank: interest spread, underwriting and property income are measured differently.
components.rubric: Latest operating margin: 4 at 25% or more, 3 at 15%, 2 at 8%, 1 at 0%, else 0; one point off when the margin has ranged more than 8 points across the years read.

components.label: Revenue growth
components.headline: Revenue compounded 10.7% a year from FY2021 to FY2025, up in 4 of 4 years.
components.rubric: Revenue growth a year, compounded over the years read: 4 at 15% or more, 3 at 8%, 2 at 3%, 1 at 0%, else 0.

components.label: Cash generation and earnings quality
components.reason: A lender's or insurer's operating cash flow moves with loans, deposits and reserves, so it says little about earnings quality.
components.rubric: Over the policy's cash-conversion window: operating cash flow against net income, and free cash flow (operating cash flow minus capex) against revenue. 4 when conversion is at least 1.0 and the free-cash-flow margin at least 15%; 3 at 0.9 and 8%; 2 at 0.7 with positive free cash flow; 1 with positive free cash flow; else 0.

components.label: Balance sheet and liquidity
components.reason: Debt is part of how a bank operates, so operating-company leverage limits do not apply; capital ratios are not read here.
components.rubric: Net debt against EBITDA and operating income against interest. 4 with net cash, or net debt at most 1x EBITDA with interest covered 8x; 3 at 2x and 5x; 2 within the policy limits (leverage_max_net_debt_ebitda, coverage_min_ebit_interest); 1 outside them; 0 when interest is covered less than 1.5x or EBITDA is negative with net debt.

components.label: Dilution and stock-based pay
components.headline: Diluted shares fell 2.1% a year over 4 years; stock-based pay was 2.0% of revenue in FY2025.
components.rubric: Diluted share count change a year and stock-based pay as a share of revenue: 4 when shares fall and stock pay is under 3%; 3 when shares rise no more than 1% a year and stock pay is under 5%; 2 at up to 3% a year with stock pay under 10%; 1 at up to 6% a year; else 0.

components.label: Durability (moat evidence)
components.headline: 3 of 3 measurable moat tests passed.
evidence: Returns above the cost of capital in at least 80% of years: passed (5 of 5 years)
Return on equity range within 6 points: passed (4.7-point range over 5 years)
Pricing power (gross margin of 40% or more): not measured (Not meaningful for this kind of business)
Revenue up in at least 75% of years without the margin falling more than 3 points: passed (up in 4 of 4 years)

These tests find the traces a durable advantage leaves in the accounts. They do not say what the advantage is (brand, network, switching costs, scale, licences); that needs the annual report and reporting, cited.

tests.test: Returns above the cost of capital in at least 80% of years
Return on equity range within 6 points
Pricing power (gross margin of 40% or more)
tests.detail: Not meaningful for this kind of business

tests.test: Revenue up in at least 75% of years without the margin falling more than 3 points

components.rubric: Moat evidence, four measurable tests, one point each: returns above the cost of capital in at least 80% of the years read; operating margin range within 6 points; gross margin of 40% or more (operating margin of 20% where gross profit is not reported); revenue up in at least 75% of years without the operating margin falling more than 3 points. Needs three tests with data. These are the traces a durable advantage leaves in the accounts; they do not say what the advantage is.

rule_of_40.reason: Applied only to companies growing revenue at least 15% a year, where trading margin for growth is the strategy; this one grew 2.8%.

quality.summary: Business quality B (3.36 of 4 across 4 measures). Strongest: dilution and stock-based pay; weakest: returns on capital.

valuation.label: Stretched

components.label: Intrinsic value
evidence: Residual income / justified price-to-book base case 238.36 a share against 334.17 (-29%).
components.reason: The residual income is a primary fit at limited confidence here, so it is shown but not graded.
components.rubric: Base-case value per share from the model that fits this business (the DCF, or residual income for a bank) against the price: 4 at 30% upside or more, 3 at +10%, 2 within 10%, 1 down to -30%, else 0. Scored only when the model is the primary fit at normal confidence.

components.label: Against its own history
components.headline: The P/E sits at the 100th percentile of its five-year range.
components.rubric: Today's P/E against the company's own five-year range: 4 in the bottom fifth, 3 below the 40th percentile, 2 below the 60th, 1 below the 80th, else 0.

components.label: Cash yield
components.reason: Free cash flow does not describe a lender's or insurer's earnings.
components.rubric: Free cash flow to equity over market value (an equity measure over an equity value), against the 10-year Treasury yield: 4 at 2 points above or more, 3 at or above it, 2 down to 1.5 below, 1 down to 3 below, else 0. Free cash flow to the firm over enterprise value is reported beside it.

components.label: What the price assumes
components.reason: Needs a reverse DCF on a primary-fit model and a revenue record.
components.rubric: Growth the price implies (reverse DCF) against the company's own revenue record: 4 when it implies 5 points a year less or more than 5 below, 3 at or below the record, 2 up to 5 above, 1 up to 10 above, else 0.

components.label: Against peers
components.headline: P/E 14.0 against a peer median of 13.7 (1.02x).
evidence: Peers: BAC, RY, WFC, C, TD, BNY, NTB, FRBT.
Market-relative: what the company would be worth at its peers' multiples. If the whole group is mispriced, so is this.
components.rubric: Trailing P/E (EV/EBITDA when earnings are negative) against the median of the peer group: 4 at 0.75x or less, 3 at 0.95x, 2 at 1.1x, 1 at 1.4x, else 0.

valuation.summary: Valuation stretched (1.00 of 4, where 4 is cheapest, across 2 measures).

chart.text: Above the 40- and 200-week averages: the long-term uptrend is intact.

volume.text: Over the last 26 weeks, volume on up weeks was 1.57x volume on down weeks, a pattern consistent with accumulation. This is an interpretation of volume, not evidence of who traded.

conviction.label: Neutral
conviction.why: Business quality B but a stretched valuation: a good business at a price that leaves little room.

accumulation.reason: No accumulation zones: conviction is Neutral, and zones are offered only at Constructive or above.

loss_paths.text: The P/E is 34% above its five-year median. If earnings hold flat for three years and the multiple returns to the median, the price falls about 25% with nothing wrong with the business.
The stock's worst fall in the history read was -44% (to 2020-03-23). A broad bear market takes good businesses down with it, and three years is short enough to end inside one.

long_term.policy_note: Business quality below B caps conviction at Neutral: a configurable rule (quality_cap_grade), not a finding.
long_term.separation_note: Business quality and valuation are graded separately: a strong business can be an expensive stock, and the chart's weakness is not by itself a failed business thesis.

setup.why: The trend is up but price is neither at a level nor back at its averages: no defined entry.

swing.why: The trend is up but price is neither at a level nor back at its averages: no defined entry.
swing.reassess_when: A pullback to the 20-day EMA near 337.38, or a daily close above the 20-day high at 355.60 on volume at least 1.5x average, would define a setup.
swing.framework_note: Grades follow this framework's stated rules (S needs aligned timeframes, reward-to-risk of 2.5 or more, no earnings in the window, a clear invalidation and outperformance of the market). They are not probabilities and have not been shown to predict returns.

eps.basis: Adjusted EPS as the Street reports it (Yahoo Finance)

revenue.reason: The pre-release revenue consensus was not saved for this quarter, and the feed replaces it once results are out.

guidance.reason: Guidance text is not in Optic's data; it is in the release and on the call.

headline_audit.reconcile_note: Consensus is on an adjusted basis; GAAP diluted EPS from the 10-Q can differ by stock pay, amortisation and one-off items. Compare like with like.

trajectory.revenue_trend_text: Revenue grew +27.7% against the same quarter a year earlier in the latest quarter, against an average of +8.6% over the two before: accelerating.

reaction.text: Gapped -1.3% at the open and faded the session so far (+0.8% on the day, +1.8% versus SPY), on 0.6x average volume.
reaction.caveat: Price and volume say how the market responded, not who bought or sold.

rubric.eps: EPS against consensus (beat +1, in line 0, miss -1; within the in-line band counts as in line)
rubric.revenue: Revenue against consensus, same scale (needs the pre-release consensus saved in a forecast)
rubric.growth_trend: Revenue growth against the prior quarters (accelerating +1, steady 0, decelerating -1)
rubric.eps_growth: EPS against the same quarter a year earlier (up +1, down -1)
rubric.margin: Operating margin against the same quarter a year earlier (up a point or more +1, down -1)
rubric.guidance: Guidance against prior guidance or consensus (raised +1, held 0, cut -1; only when known)

quality.note: Graded on the report, not on the stock's reaction. One criterion cannot decide it: a marginal miss inside the in-line band scores zero, not minus one.

positives: Revenue grew +27.7% against the same quarter a year earlier in the latest quarter, against an average of +8.6% over the two before: accelerating.
red_flags: None found within the reviewed evidence.

forecast_review.reason: No pre-release forecast was saved for this quarter, so there is nothing to score; one is saved automatically whenever a pre-earnings analysis runs.

next_quarter.watch: Whether revenue growth holds against the trend above, and the next-quarter estimate revisions in the weeks after this report.

post.separation_note: The grade describes the report. The reaction describes the stock. They often disagree, and both can be right.

lines: Long term: Neutral (business quality B, valuation stretched).
Swing: No Setup. The trend is up but price is neither at a level nor back at its averages: no defined entry.
Earnings just reported (2026-10-13): report quality B; Gapped -1.3% at the open and faded the session so far (+0.8% on the day, +1.8% versus SPY), on 0.6x average volume.
combined.verdict: Neither the long-term case nor the trade stands out on the evidence here.
combined.note: Each assessment answers its own question; none is averaged into the others.
